result.topic_en: Heat conduction with a time-varying boundary temperature φ(t): Riemann writes the temperature u as a Duhamel-type integral, makes it explicit using the error-function kernel χ(x,t), changes variables, and rewrites it with φ′ under the integral, which also covers jumps in the boundary temperature.

Temperature as a superposition (Duhamel) integral of the boundary temperature φ
Fundamental solution for a unit step in boundary temperature (complementary error function) and its time derivative

Change of variables in the solution integral
Substitution used for the change of variables
Treatment of jumps in the boundary temperature: add a term χ(x,t−τ) times the jump at each jump time

items.english: To apply this formula to the case where the functions change by jumps, at every instant τ where the temperature changes one must add to the integral a term χ(x,t−τ) multiplied by the increment of the temperature at that instant.
